lessons.content:
PAGE_1:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 1 8 Ideas for Increasing Your Digital Book Sales

PAGE_2:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 2 Marketing and promoting your non-fiction Kindle eBook is just as important as actually getting the writing done. You should have a plan in place as soon as the writing is done so that you can implement it. This is how you get your expertise out there and establish yourself as an authority in your market. A marketing plan may sound a bit daunting, but when broken down it’s quite simple. The idea is to let the people who could use your book know about it. You just need to engage with potential readers, tell them why they'd like your book, and inspire them to buy it. A marketing plan consists of strategies you can implement to let people know about your book. Here are 8 ideas that you can easily implement online.  1.     Advanced Social Media It's a given that you should use Facebook and Twitter to promote your eBook. These are the biggest social media sites and your potential audience is sure to be using them. But you can go beyond these two and explore some other social media platforms that are excellent for promotion. Instagram and Pinterest are two visual social media platforms that have become increasingly popular in recent years. They both allow you to share images, and Pinterest lets you create themed "boards." Some things you can do with these sites include: Ø Create a hashtag for your book and encourage people to use it Ø Share your book cover or images of your book Ø Turn your book's tips into visual content Ø Take pictures of you or others implementing your book's tips Ø Share images from promotional events

PAGE_3:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 3 2.     Host a Virtual Book Tour A virtual book tour is essentially the same as a traditional book tour. The idea is to get out there and meet your readers, talk about your book, and help build buzz for it. The difference is that with a virtual tour, you do it all online. The benefit of a virtual book tour is that it takes little in the way of resources, but the possibilities are limitless. You can do everything through free or cheap online tours, and reach an even bigger audience than you could offline. A virtual book tour could include any or all of the following: Ø Guest blog posts to coincide with your book launch Ø Readings where you talk about the book  Ø Interviews on podcasts, YouTube channels, or social media that discuss your book Ø Free giveaways through your blog, others’ blogs, or sites like Goodreads  3.     Get Your Readers to Promote Your Book Give advance copies to your customers and ask them for honest reviews. Offer a free book giveaway to a limited number of customers in exchange for their review. Reviews work as a form of social proof. When people read reviews about your book from others, not you, it has a more powerful effect. It’s important that you ask for honest reviews. Don’t ask your customers to only say good things about your book. If all of the reviews say it’s the best book they’ve ever read, your reviews will look fake.

PAGE_4:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 4 You might want to consider identifying influencers in your niche and reaching out to them for reviews in particular. Find blogs that have a following or people active on social media and give them a copy.  4.     Create a Promotional Video for Your Book It takes a bit of work to create a promotional video, but a video is quick and easy to digest and video content performs particularly well on social media. You can create a video that's simply you talking to the camera. You can also outsource video production if you really want to get it done with little to no fuss. Share your “book trailer” on social media, YouTube and other video sharing sites, your author website or blog, and on your Amazon Author Page. Other ways to share your book trailer include sending it in an email to your list, sharing it at offline events, adding it to social media profiles, and sharing it on book websites like Goodreads and I Love Book Trailers.  5.     Promote Your Book in Your Email Signature Add a blurb about your book in your email signature, and everyone who receives an email from you will also get your promotional message. Make the message short and quick, emphasizing the benefits of the information you share in the book. Include a link to more information on your book or, better yet, a place where they can buy it. The best way to do this is by creating an Amazon Author Page URL and posting it here. This is a personalized web address that goes straight to your author page on Amazon. You can learn about making one here.

PAGE_5:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 5 6.     Network with Other Authors in Writing Communities Connect with other writers and network with them. You can find beta readers to review your book, swap reviews, and learn some writing and publishing tips. It’s wonderful just to have a community of writers to support and encourage you when you need it as well. Many forums and groups focus more on fiction or certain genres, so make sure you connect with a community that serves your goals. A few communities include: Ø KBoards (for Kindle users and authors) Ø Non-Fiction Author Association Ø Writing Forums Ø BookRix Forum  7.     Find Book Review Bloggers Conduct a Google search with the name of your book or its genre followed by search terms such as “book reviews,” “book review blogger,” or “book blogger.” Before you approach bloggers, carefully read their review policy. When you approach them, write a personal email and give them whatever information they need to know such as your book’s topic and what format you can send it in. Keep in mind that you may not get a good review from a reviewer. However, reviews that aren’t totally positive are authentic and can still help you promote your book. You can also ask book bloggers who regularly interview writers for an interview.

PAGE_6:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 6 8.     Get Your Book on Goodreads Goodreads is the world’s largest website for readers and book recommendations and is owned by Amazon. This is a website where book lovers indulge in their shared passion for reading, so it’s not a place for promoting books. Keep this in mind and don’t jump in and promote heavily. If you’re going to use Goodreads for future books, sign up for a profile and start using it as a user first. Create your profile, join relevant groups, and participate in discussions. You can create an author page, advertise your book through the site, add your book to relevant lists, or create discussions or Q&A sessions about your book.  Make Your Book Visible The key to selling your book and spreading your expertise is to make your book visible. Find your audience and put your book in front of them. This is all you need for an easy and effective marketing plan.
